findings.description: A long-lived AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in cleartext in the Lambda function's environment variables and committed to source control. Anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration or repository read access can retrieve them and impersonate the associated IAM principal.

No kms_key_arn is set, so environment variables holding secrets are protected only by the default AWS-managed Lambda key, which grants decryption to any principal able to read the function configuration. A customer-managed CMK with a restrictive key policy would add a separate access-control boundary around these secrets.

The function uses nodejs12.x, which is past end-of-life and no longer receives security patches from AWS, leaving the execution environment exposed to unpatched vulnerabilities in the runtime and its dependencies.
